description: ADR-0020 §7 + least-privilege capability for the MAIN Tauri window (the dashboard / settings UI). This is the trust boundary for the privileged renderer — it can dispatch IPC to the Python sidecar, spawn / kill the sidecar binary (spawning is owned by the Rust host via ``app.shell().sidecar()`` — not ACL-gated), post notifications, read/write the clipboard (long-text paste path), open save-file dialogs, and own the system tray. Every permission is explicit (Tauri v2 ships zero permissions by default). SEC-026 regression fix: this file was split out of the original migrate-runtime.json so the BUBBLE window (a sandboxed renderer that only renders the audio-level pill) gets its own minimal capability (bubble-runtime.json) instead of inheriting the main window's full grant. The bubble renderer must NOT be able to invoke shell:spawn, clipboard write, dialog save, or tray operations even if it is compromised (XSS in the waveform renderer). Permissions granted: (1) core window/event/webview defaults for the main window; (2) shell:allow-spawn + kill — the JS-facing spawn scope is the plugin default (deny-all): the webview cannot spawn anything; all sidecar/worker spawning is owned by the Rust host via app.shell().sidecar(), which is not ACL-gated (tauri-plugin-shell v2 config accepts only an `open` key — the former plugins.shell.scope block crashed app startup with 'unknown field `scope`'); (3) notification + clipboard-manager + dialog for the toast/paste/export paths; (4) the tauri-plugin-single-instance gate does NOT require a capability grant — it is a non-scoped plugin registered via `.plugin(tauri_plugin_single_instance::init(...))` in main.rs (ADR-0020 §7 + Phase 4 — the second instance is routed to focus the first window instead of launching a duplicate); (5) core:tray:default ONLY — the Rust host OWNS the system tray (tauri-plugin-tray / core tray-icon feature, ADR-0020 §6.5) and renders it directly via Tauri's built-in tray API; the main renderer never manipulates the tray. the previous `core:tray:allow-set-icon` / `allow-set-tooltip` / `allow-set-title` / `allow-set-menu` / `allow-new` / `allow-remove-by-id` / `allow-get-by-id` grants were dropped because the renderer does not invoke any tray-manipulation IPC — the Python sidecar computes the menu structure and emits a `tray_menu` event; the Rust host renders it and routes clicks back via `dispatch({cmd:'tray_click',data:{id}})` (pystray is the Electron-fallback path only and is never used under Tauri). `core:tray:default` is retained so the renderer can still observe tray-related events broadcast by the Rust host. supervisor full-app relaunch uses AppHandle::restart() (core tauri crate, no plugin required), so no process:allow-restart capability is needed. ADR-0020 §15: tauri-plugin-updater is intentionally NOT granted any permissions — auto-update is out of scope for v1 (see docs/migration/signing-guide.md §'No auto-update').
